references.text: Isaiah describes how the suffering servant will be 'highly exalted' (Hebrew: *nissah*), a concept that Jesus directly links to his own crucifixion and exaltation in John 12:32.

In this verse, Jesus explicitly refers to Moses and the serpent in the wilderness and connects the 'exaltation' of the Son to salvation for all, which is the direct theological basis for the statement in John 12:32.

Jesus repeats the motif of being 'highly exalted' (*hypsōthō*) and links it to the recognition that he is the Messiah, a direct parallel to the statement in 12:32 that his exaltation will draw all people to himself.
Paul describes how God has 'highly exalted' Jesus after his obedience unto death, so that every knee should bow to him, fulfilling Jesus' prophecy that his exaltation will draw all people to himself.
